intent: End-to-end script for the annotated adoption path

title: Failure-injection steps must prove the fault took effect before asserting survival
why: The first corruption test zeroed bytes that were already zero in the CDS archive, so fetch accepted it and the test proved nothing. The step now overwrites random bytes, compares SHA-256 before and after, and aborts if unchanged.
alternative: Trust the dd exit status - rejected: it succeeded while changing nothing

title: A changed JVM option is a new fingerprint, tested as such (uncached, retrained, rollback hits the old archive)
why: The injector passes --jvm-arg to fetch and the trainer, so a changed option finds no archive at fetch rather than being caught later by the run wrapper. The test follows what the injector really does.
alternative: Assert the chart path's 'archive does not match this launch' log - rejected: wrong for the injected path, as the first run showed

title: Start-to-Ready is reported from pod conditions and the JVM's own figure, never gated
why: Pod conditions have 1 s resolution and the example app starts in under a second, so pod-level times show no difference; the JVM-reported figure does (0.48 s vs 0.31 s median). kind timings are too noisy for a CI threshold.
alternative: Fail CI below a speedup threshold - rejected: would flake and would measure a toy app

title: New script and own CI job (amd64 and arm64) instead of extending e2e-kind.sh
why: The chart path and the annotated path must not hide each other's failures; Helm 3 is pinned because the post-renderer is a script path. The arm64 runner job has not run yet and is documented as unverified.
alternative: Extend the 190-line chart-specific script - rejected: coupling and masked failures
